question: How many chambers are there in the heart of fishes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fishes have a **two-chambered heart** consisting of one atrium and one ventricle.
 
• The blood flows in a single circuit, from the heart to the gills for oxygenation and then to the rest of the body.
 
• The two-chambered heart is efficient for the aquatic life of fishes, supporting their metabolism and oxygen needs.
 
• Having a two-chambered heart is a characteristic feature of **most fish species**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chambers of the Heart**

 
 
• **Atrium:** The atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body and sends it to the ventricle.
 
• **Ventricle:** The ventricle pumps the deoxygenated blood to the gills for oxygenation.
 
 
 
• **Circulatory System in Fishes**
 
 
• Fishes have a **single circulatory system**, meaning blood passes through the heart only once during each complete circuit of the body.
 
• After oxygenation in the gills, the oxygen-rich blood is delivered directly to the tissues without returning to the heart.
 
• This system is different from mammals and birds, which have a double circulatory system.
 
 
 
• **Gills**
 
 
• Gills are the respiratory organs in fishes that allow them to extract oxygen from water.
 
• Blood flows through the gill filaments where gas exchange occurs – carbon dioxide is released into the water and oxygen is absorbed.
 
 
 
• **Adaptations**
 
 
• The two-chambered heart and single circulatory system are highly adapted to an aquatic environment where oxygen levels can vary.
 
• These adaptations ensure efficient oxygen delivery to support the metabolism and activity levels of fishes.
